title: Permit-Required Confined Space Entry
summary: A permit-required confined space is hard to enter or exit and has a hazard such as bad air, engulfment, or entrapment. Entry needs a written program, a signed permit, an attendant outside, and a rescue plan.
talking_points: A permit space is large enough to enter, not made for continuous occupancy, has limited entry or exit, and has a serious hazard such as a hazardous atmosphere, engulfment, or a trapping shape.
Never enter a permit space without a permit signed by the entry supervisor and a written program in place.
Test the air before entry and monitor it during entry, in this order: oxygen, combustible gases or vapors, then toxic gases or vapors.
If hazardous conditions are detected during entry, leave the space immediately.
At least one attendant must stay outside for the whole entry. The attendant keeps count of entrants, keeps contact, and does no other duties.
Entrants wear a chest or full body harness with a retrieval line attached, and use the required PPE.
The attendant summons rescue. Untrained people must not attempt a rescue, and rescuers must be trained in first aid and CPR.
Exit right away if ordered to, if you see warning signs or symptoms of exposure, if a prohibited condition exists, or if an alarm goes off.
site_hazards_to_check: Missing danger signs at permit space entrances
No posted permit, or permit not signed or already expired
No atmosphere test results, or testing not done in order (oxygen, combustibles, toxics)
No attendant stationed outside the space
No harness and retrieval line, or no ventilation, lighting, and communication equipment
No rescue service arranged, or no way to summon it
discussion_questions: What makes this space a permit space, and what are its hazards?
Who is the attendant, and what are they never allowed to do?
When must an entrant leave the space immediately?

attribution.notice: Adapted from OSHA published material. Reproduced with attribution for jobsite safety training; not an endorsement by OSHA.

flags: Verified every point against OSHA 3138 (permit-required confined spaces): permit space definition, signed permit by entry supervisor, testing order oxygen/combustibles/toxics, leave immediately on hazardous conditions, attendant outside with no other duties, harness and retrieval line, rescue summoned by attendant, rescuers trained in first aid and CPR, exit triggers.

FIX: removed 29 CFR 1910.146. OSHA 3138 explicitly describes the general-industry standard; the construction equivalent is 29 CFR 1926 Subpart AA (1926.1200-1213), which exists and covers the same elements (permit, attendant, atmospheric testing, retrieval, rescue). 1926 Subpart AA retained as the mapping.

Non-blocking: source describes 1910.146 requirements; Subpart AA adds construction-specific duties not in this talk (competent person, continuous atmospheric monitoring, early-warning for engulfment, host/controlling contractor coordination). Foremen should treat this as an awareness talk, not a compliance program, and consult the site's written entry program.
Non-blocking: 'Never enter without a permit' is stated as absolute; correct for permit-required spaces (alternate procedures exist only under the standard's specific conditions).
